MIS-01|A horizontal speed-time segment means constant speed; it does not mean the object is at rest as a horizontal distance-time segment does.|2.3.2:8|2025,2,1(a),at rest|Show one horizontal speed graph and one horizontal distance graph and ask which object changes position.

MIS-02|Distance comes from speed-time area; acceleration comes from gradient.|2.3.3:5,2.3.3:3|2025,1,5,gradient of the graph|Give one speed-time plot and ask for a distance and an acceleration with units that distinguish the operations.

MIS-03|Average speed is total distance divided by total elapsed time, not an unweighted average of speeds.|2.3.2:5|2024,2,1(e),added the speeds|Compare unequal-duration journey legs where the arithmetic mean of the speeds gives a different answer.

MIS-04|Constant velocity requires zero resultant force; a nonzero driving force can be balanced by resistance.|2.4:1|2023,2,2(a),120 N|Specify a steady pulled object and ask separately for the pulling force and the net force.

MIS-05|Moment uses perpendicular distance from pivot to force line; work uses displacement along the force.|2.7:2|2023,2,4(a),scalar and vector|Use a pivoted lever and a translating block and require the relevant distance in each calculation.

MIS-06|Mass is retained when gravitational field strength changes; weight is not.|2.5:1,2.5:6|2023,1,10,confusion between mass and weight|Move an object between two specified gravitational fields and compare both quantities.

MIS-07|Momentum conservation is conditional on no external resultant force, not an unconditional property of every moving system.|2.4:11|2022,2,5(a),condition|Contrast an isolated collision with a system receiving an external impulse and require the governing condition.

MIS-08|Opposing velocities carry opposite signs when adding momenta.|2.4:12|2022,2,5(b),one of the velocities should be negative|Compare head-on and same-direction collisions with the same speed magnitudes and ask for signed initial momentum.

MIS-09|Specific latent heat concerns phase change per unit mass; specific heat capacity concerns temperature rise per unit mass.|3.2.2:10,3.2.2:5|2024,1,13,specific heat capacity|Contrast heating within one phase with melting at constant temperature and select the physical quantity for each.

MIS-10|Energy supplied during a constant-temperature phase change changes intermolecular potential energy rather than increasing average kinetic energy.|3.2.2:11|2024,2,3(c),kinetic energy|Compare one sloping and one flat heating-curve section and ask which energy store changes.

MIS-11|Conduction at a heater boundary and convection through a fluid are different transfer processes.|3.3.1:1,3.3.2:3|2020,2,4(a)(i),convection instead of conduction|Ask separately how energy crosses a metal-water boundary and then spreads through the bulk water.

MIS-12|Reflection returns light at a boundary; refraction changes its propagation through media.|4.3.3:2,4.3.3:7|2022,2,6(a),Refraction and Reflection|Use two original ray paths and require the process at each boundary rather than the name of the apparatus.

MIS-13|A real image is formed where rays actually converge; a virtual image is located by their backward extensions.|4.3.3:13|2022,2,7(a)(i),virtual and real image|Ask which of two ray constructions can form an image on a screen and explain why.
MIS-14|Incidence and refraction angles are measured to the normal, not to the surface.|4.3.3:4|2024,2,4(d)(i),given angle|Provide an angle to the surface and require the angle used in the sine ratio.

MIS-15|Frequency and period are reciprocals, not interchangeable numerical inputs to the wave-speed equation.|4.1:9|2022,2,8(b),substituted the period|Give period and wavelength, require speed, and ask why multiplying the supplied values directly is wrong.
MIS-16|Sound loudness follows amplitude rather than wavelength.|4.4:5|2025,1,25,decrease in wavelength|Compare two sound traces with equal period and different amplitudes and ask which is quieter.

MIS-17|Positive charging is explained by electron loss; protons are not transferred in the rubbing model.|5.1:1,5.1:8|2025,1,28,loss of electrons|Track electron transfer between initially neutral insulating objects and infer both final signs.

MIS-18|Resistances in parallel cannot simply be added as series resistances.|5.3:7|2023,1,31,added up|Present an original mixed circuit and require the student to identify the parallel group before calculating.

MIS-19|Work per charge is potential difference; work per time is power.|5.2.2:3,5.4:1|2025,1,30,work done divided by time|Give one energy transfer, one charge and one time and ask for the two physically different ratios and units.

MIS-20|Slip rings in an alternating generator and a split-ring commutator in a motor serve different contact functions.|5.7.2.2:1,5.7.1.2:4|2024,2,7(b),split ring|Compare two original contact arrangements and ask which reverses coil current and which preserves rotating contact connections.

MIS-21|Transformer induction requires a changing magnetic field linking the secondary, not merely a definition of alternating current.|5.7.2.3:1|2023,2,9(a),changing magnetic field|Contrast steady and alternating primary current and require a causal account through core flux to secondary electromotive force.

MIS-22|Nucleon number counts protons plus neutrons; it is not the neutron count alone.|6.1.1:3,6.1.1:1|2024,1,39,nucleons|Give an original nuclide and ask separately for nucleons, protons and neutrons.

MIS-23|Isotopes share proton number and differ in neutron/nucleon number; those roles cannot be exchanged.|6.1.2:1|2025,2,9(b),interchanged|Present pairs with different proton and neutron counts and ask which pair can be isotopes of one element.

MIS-24|Spring extension is loaded length minus original length, not the loaded length itself.|2.4:5,2.4:6|2025,1,10,extension|Give original and loaded spring lengths and ask for both extension and stiffness.

MIS-25|A cooling rate is temperature change per elapsed time, not an average temperature.|3.2.3:4,1.1:2|2021,3,1(c)(iii),average temperature|Provide initial/final temperatures and elapsed time and ask for the rate with a derived unit.

MIS-26|Attraction alone does not prove that a metal object is a permanent magnet; repulsion of one pole does.|5.6:1|2023,1,34,conclusive proof|Compare attraction-only and attraction-plus-repulsion observations and ask which identifies a permanent magnet.

MIS-27|Graph gradient is change in vertical quantity divided by change in horizontal quantity, with the sign retained.|1.2.3:9|2020,3,3(c)(ii),swopped|Use a decreasing straight line with unlike axis units and ask for gradient sign, magnitude and unit.
MIS-28|Absolute zero is zero kelvin, not zero degrees Celsius.|3.2.1:1|2024,1,16,0°C|Ask the student to compare freezing-point and absolute-zero temperatures on both scales.

MIS-29|A micrometer's usual external measuring faces cannot measure the inside diameter as vernier internal jaws can.|2.1:2|2024,1,1,internal|Give an internal ring diameter and an external wire diameter and require a suitable instrument for each.
